title: Eludite agent permission policy
description: The per-solution, committable permission policy for hosted agents (PLAN.md 5.3), in `.eludite/agents-policy.json` beside the solution file. Class `read` always runs and is not configurable, except where `browser`, `debug` or `git` refuses a call outright. Every key is optional; a missing file is the defaults. Eludite rewrites the file when the user answers a permission prompt with Always Allow (adding a rule); it keeps unknown keys out and writes the keys sorted, so the file diffs cleanly.

edit_buffer.description: Agent edits of files: `review` (default) holds them as pending changes until accepted or rejected; `accept` applies them at once (still audited).

execute.description: Build, test, run, shell commands, unknown tools: `prompt` (default), `allow` or `deny`, unless a rule matches.

dangerous.description: Push, delete, external network: `prompt` (default) or `deny`, unless a rule matches.

rules.description: Decisions for specific tools, checked in order before the class default (execute and dangerous only). The first matching rule wins.

tool.description: The tool as the agent names it: an agent tool (`Bash`, `WebFetch`) or an Eludite MCP tool (`mcp__eludite__eludite-solution-open`, or just `eludite-solution-open`).

command_prefix.description: Only when the tool's `command` argument (a shell command) starts with this text.

browser.description: The browser commands (eludite.browser.*; brief 0024, ADR-0009). Every key is optional; a missing key is its default.

origins.description: Where an agent may send the browser without the call becoming dangerous (eludite.browser.navigate and tab_open with a url, open_external). Each entry is a host (`localhost`, `[::1]`, `*.example.com` for the domain and its subdomains) or a host and port (`localhost:5000`), for http and https; an origin (`https://example.com`: that scheme and host on any port; `https://example.com:8443`: that port only); a `file:///` path (file urls under it); `$workspace` (file urls under the workspace folder); or `$launch_urls` (the `applicationUrl`s of the workspace's `Properties/launchSettings.json` profiles). Absent: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `$workspace` and `$launch_urls`. `about:` urls are always allowed. Always Allow on an off-origin navigation adds its origin here, writing the defaults first when the list was absent, and keeps the list sorted.

network_bodies.description: eludite.browser.network_body: `allow` (default) or `deny` (agents are refused, with this policy named).

evaluate.description: eludite.browser.evaluate: `allow` (default: class execute), `prompt` (class dangerous, which prompts) or `deny` (agents are refused, with this policy named).

debug.description: The debugger commands (eludite.debug.*; proposal 0001 section 5.5, brief 0027, ADR-0009). Every key is optional; a missing key is its default. Reads (state, snapshot, stack, variables, output, exception_info, wait, processes) are always allowed. `prompt` makes a call dangerous (the Agents window asks; Always Allow writes `allow` here), `deny` refuses agents with this policy named. The tool rules above are checked first and keep working for finer control.

drive.description: Whether agents may start sessions (start, attach, restart) and resume or change them (continue, step_over, step_into, step_out, run_to_cursor, run_until, trace, pause, stop, set_variable, set_next_statement, toggle_breakpoint with a `log_message` expression): `allow` (default: each call keeps its class, execute), `prompt` (dangerous) or `deny`.

attach.description: eludite.debug.attach to a process Eludite did not start: `prompt` (default: dangerous, which asks) or `deny` (agents are refused any attach).

evaluate.description: Whether agents may run debuggee code through expressions: eludite.debug.evaluate, set_variable, and tracepoints whose message has an `{expression}` (toggle_breakpoint's `log_message`, trace's points): `allow` (default), `prompt` (dangerous) or `deny`.

git.description: The git commands (eludite.git.*; brief 0040, ADR-0009). Every key is optional; a missing key is its default. Reads (status, diff, log, branches, blame, the stash and worktree lists) are always allowed; staging, checkout, merge, cherry-pick, stash, fetch, pull and worktree changes are class execute; discarding changes, `reset` with `hard` and dropping a stash are class dangerous. `prompt` makes a call dangerous (the Agents window asks; Always Allow writes a tool rule for it), `deny` refuses agents with this policy named; the tool rules above are checked first. A `force` (checkout, push, branch delete, worktree remove) is refused for agents whatever this says.

commit.description: eludite.git.commit without `amend`: `allow` (default: class execute, decided by `execute` and the rules), `prompt` (dangerous) or `deny`.

history.description: Calls that rewrite or move history: eludite.git.commit with `amend`, eludite.git.reset, eludite.git.rebase, eludite.git.pull with `rebase`, eludite.git.merge with `abort`: `prompt` (default: dangerous) or `deny`.
